items.statement: Final: different productive reactivity of the two configurations
items.expected: In the final conclusion, connect the two validly mapped sets of reaction states and the lower TS20-a to its more favorable productive C–H activation, providing a computationally supported explanation of stereodifferentiation. The 8.6 numerical window need not be passed, but the direction and relevant reaction must be supported by actual results. Do not assert exactly zero reaction through the higher channel, an unmapped absolute configuration, rate control over the full cycle or an exact experimental endpoint ee. An equivalent mechanistic explanation supported by executed work is acceptable.

items.statement: Final: configurational stability under separate conditions and the limits of DKR inference
items.expected: In the final conclusion, use the computed S/P inversions, their respective minima/solvents/temperatures and corresponding positive barriers to explain that configurational interconversion of the isolated molecules is limited by thermal activation, and relate this to the time courses and observed product stability within explicit bounds. Numerical ordering under separate conditions cannot establish kinetic ordering under identical conditions, rapid S interconversion at 363.15 K/MeCN/36 h or a closed quantitative DKR model. Genuine results for both molecules must support this scientific judgment; a P value outside its numerical window does not automatically invalidate it. Coordinated-state interconversion, a full cycle or exact ee is not required.
